finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: The prompt’s target is an active volcano at Ross Island in Antarctica: GVP identifies Erebus as the southernmost active volcano in Antarctica and locates it on Ross Island (L80,L116); retained BAS also labels Mount Erebus as Ross Island (L43@P1). GVP profiles ground the alternatives: Etna in Italy’s Sicily Volcanic Province with recent confirmed activity (Italy page L56-L63,L75); Fuji is a volcano on Honshu (Fujisan page L105); Kilimanjaro is a volcanic massif of three edifices in Tanzania (Kilimanjaro page L318-L320). Only Erebus fits the requested place.
finalGroupBindings.locator: GVP Erebus L80,L116-L117; BAS L43@P1; GVP Italy L56-L63,L75; Fujisan L105; Kilimanjaro L318-L320.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Это Эребус. В его кратере долго существует лавовое озеро.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: GVP reports the active lava lake in Erebus’s summit crater since at least 1972 (L80,L116-L117,L667-L668), supporting the explanation’s crater/lava-lake claim.
finalGroupBindings.locator: GVP Erebus L80,L116-L117; the persistent lava lake is also described at L667-L668.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Этна — действующий вулкан на итальянском острове Сицилия.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: GVP classifies Etna in the Sicily Volcanic Province of Italy (L62) and reports confirmed eruptions into 2026 (L75); this substantiates the note’s Sicilian location and active-volcano description.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Эребус на острове Росса — самый южный действующий вулкан Земли.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: GVP identifies Erebus as the southernmost active volcano and locates it on Ross Island (L80,L116), facts beyond the prompt’s place clue and the answer name.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Фудзи — вулканическая вершина на японском острове Хонсю.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: GVP’s Fujisan profile identifies Fuji as a volcano and its map caption explicitly places Fuji on Honshu Island (L105), matching the note.
finalGroupBindings.locator: GVP Fujisan profile, map caption L105.

finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: GVP describes Kilimanjaro as a massif formed by three volcanic edifices (L318) and identifies it as Tanzania’s volcano (L319), supporting the note.
